figures.caption: Pipeline of the project: run_all.sh orchestrates the C++17 simulator (event-driven hard-sphere MD with collision Verlet and Ewald/DSF Coulomb), which writes the trajectory as extended XYZ plus an npz cache, JSON metadata and a per-frame diagnostics CSV; sim/analyze.py scans every frame for overlaps and computes energy drift and pairing statistics, while render_ovito.py (Tachyon ray tracer, numpy fallback) produces 721 PNG frames per movie that ffmpeg encodes to H.264 mp4.

Collision Verlet (Houndonougbo, Laird & Leimkuhler 2000) as implemented. (a) The +/− Coulomb pair potential φc = −l_B/r (l_B = 5 σ) is split into a long-range part φ₂ that follows the Hermite cubic P(r) on [q₁, q₂] = [1, 1.5] σ and is flat at P(q₁) = −3.70 kT inside q₁, and a short-range part φ₁ = φc − φ₂ that vanishes beyond q₂; the hard core r < σ is shaded. (b) The corresponding pair forces: F₂ and its slope vanish at contact, F₁ carries the full contact force −5 kT/σ and goes to zero continuously at q₂. (c) One step h: outer half-kicks with F₂, exact hard-sphere propagation in between in which every hard collision (anywhere in the system) cuts the step into velocity-Verlet sub-steps with F₁; accelerated ions follow parabolic paths and their collision times are the smallest positive root of the quartic |Δq + Δvτ + ½Δaτ²|² = σ². The shipped cv-phys variant reflects the physical velocity v + F₂(τᵢ − h/2) at each collision instead of the drift velocity.

Energy-error order test on the production system (N = 1000, η = 0.35, 20+/20−, l_B = 5 σ): maximum |E(t) − E(0)|/N over 2 τ of NVE dynamics versus the step h for the four integrators, with the fitted log–log slopes in the legends and dashed reference lines ∝ h and ∝ h². (a) Equilibrated start (15 τ with charges on): the shipped cv-phys is second order (slope 2.02) whereas the literal HLL collision Verlet is only sub-first-order (slope 0.73) and 35× less accurate at the production step h = 0.005 τ; kdk-phys gives 1.82 and the naive splitting 1.09. (b) Same test from the un-equilibrated start with Ewald (solid; slopes 1.40 / 0.78 / 1.69 / 0.89) and with the smooth DSF Coulomb model (dashed, cv-phys 1.92, cv 1.21). The Ewald real-space truncation erfc(αr_c) ≈ 7.5×10⁻⁵ gives an energy floor of ≈ 0.5–1 × 10⁻⁶ kT/N that limits the cv-phys curve at h = 0.0025 τ (local slope 1.0 between 0.005 and 0.0025 τ; 6 × 10⁻⁷ kT/N in (a)); cv and naive are flat there because of their own first-order collision error (65× and 229× above the floor, local slopes 0.11 and −0.06), and kdk-phys is not yet affected (local slope 2.9).

test_setup.ewald_floor_note: approximate; cv-phys reaches 6e-7 in (a), so the floor is 0.5-1e-6 kT/N and limits cv-phys only
test_setup.slope_rounding: slope_fit = round(fit, 3) is a numbers entry only; captions are formatted from the unrounded fit

figures.caption: Stills taken from the three movies (frames 0, 360 and 720 of 721, i.e. t = 0, 9 and 18 τ of the NVE production run; the camera orbits from azimuth 25° to 65° over the movie): (a) the neutral control (1000 hard spheres, η = 0.35), (b) the charged run in the opaque CPK style (20 red + and 20 blue − ions, l_B = 5 σ), of which only the ions near the three camera-facing faces are visible, and (c) the same charged frames in the x-ray style with the neutrals 85 % transparent, which shows all 40 ions and their contact pairs inside the box.

Close-ups of the charged production run in the x-ray style of the movie (neutrals 85 % transparent, ions opaque; red +, blue −), re-rendered at 3× the movie resolution for the three frames chosen from a cluster scan with the r < 1.2 σ contact criterion: (a) an isolated +/− contact pair at the front face of the box at t = 16.27 τ (nearest other ion 2.5 σ away, no other ion inside the circle in projection, no neutral in front of it), (b) a linear four-ion chain (+ − + −) at t = 9.75 τ and (c) a linear five-ion chain (− + − + −) at t = 9.22 τ, 42 σ from the camera. Dotted circles enclose the cluster; the bar gives 1 σ at the depth of the cluster. Such chains are transient: clusters of four or more ions exist in 142 of the 721 frames and the largest cluster seen has six ions.

scan.six_ion_clusters_note: all 8 six-ion clusters (frames 527-535) are branched (max degree 3) and sit 48 sigma deep behind ~115 neutrals; the clean linear 5-ion chain of frames 368-370 is shown instead

render.id_convention: member_particle_indices are 0-based npz/array indices (FORMAT.md order); member_xyz_ids = index + 1 are the 1-based id column of the extended XYZ

figures.caption: Rendering cost per 1280×720 frame on the 4-core Xeon box (no GPU), measured on the 1000-sphere test trajectory including overlay and PNG writing: OVITO/Tachyon cpk at final quality (16 ambient-occlusion samples, 16 Tachyon threads) takes 1.43 s per frame, i.e. ≈ 17 min for a 721-frame movie, the x-ray preset 1.27 s (≈ 15 min), the AO-free draft preset 0.26 s (≈ 3 min) and the numpy fallback renderer with 4 worker processes 0.24 s wall (≈ 3 min). The annotated vertical ticks mark the three production movies: 1028 s and 1031 s wall for render plus encode of the two cpk movies (1.43 s per frame, two coinciding ticks) and 896 s for the x-ray movie (1.24 s per frame).

numbers.cpu: 4 x Intel Xeon 2.10 GHz, no GPU

notes: fig_stills is 7.2 x 6.9 in instead of the requested ~7.2 x 4.3 in: three rows of near-square box crops (640 x 622 px each) cannot fit a 4.3 in tall full-width figure without shrinking the spheres below legibility; the per-figure height convention (2.4-4.5 in) is therefore exceeded for this one figure.

The DSF order-test data come from traj/_test/cv_confirmer_order/dsf_order.csv (identical copies exist in traj/_test/cv_impl and traj/_test/cv_fixer_order); only the cv-phys and cv DSF curves are drawn in fig_order(b) to keep the panel readable, the kdk-phys and naive DSF slopes are in the numbers.

The integrator palette of figstyle (C_INTEG) is kept as required; because the gray "naive" entry and the orange/green pair are weak under colour-vision deficiency, every integrator additionally has its own marker shape and the slopes are printed in the legend.

fig_pair_closeup: the three frames (651, 390, 369) were re-rendered with render/render_ovito.py at 3840 x 2160 (3x the movie, x-ray style, final quality, no overlay) into traj/_test/report/closeup_frames/ (scratch), so the 900 x 792 px crops are shown at ~390 dpi; the camera pose is that of the movie frame. Panel (c) uses the linear 5-ion chain of frame 369 (42 sigma deep, 29 neutrals in front) instead of frame 512 (48 sigma, 128 neutrals in front); all six-ion clusters are branched and 48 sigma deep. Particle ids in its numbers are given both as 0-based npz indices (member_particle_indices) and 1-based extended-XYZ ids (member_xyz_ids).

fig_order caption: the ~1e-6 kT/N Ewald truncation floor limits only cv-phys at h = 0.0025 tau (local slope 1.0); cv and naive are flat there because of their own first-order collision error (65x and 229x above the floor); slopes in the captions are formatted from the unrounded log-log fits (slope_fit in numbers is rounded to 3 decimals).
Every in-figure text of the method figures is >= 8 pt.
